moduleTitle: Exporting test lists and results in Tricentis Testim
learningObjectives: Export execution run results to CSV from the Test Runs view.
Generate a shareable PDF report of test run results.

elements.description: CSV exports apply the chosen view/filter scope. Execution Runs exports executions; Test Runs exports individual runs (CSV is documented only for Counted Runs); Test Library exports test metadata, not the same result table. For Test Runs, the visible 200-result default does not truncate the matching CSV results. The export guide documents professional-plan entitlement.

The result editor’s three-dot menu offers Generate PDF run report. Share it as a report of the selected run, not proof of complete requirement/code coverage or all project tests. The export does not execute or edit tests.

bulletPoints: Select the correct view/filter and entitlement for CSV export.
Counted Test Runs CSV includes matching results beyond the visible 200 default.
PDF run reports share the selected run; they do not certify complete coverage.

examPitfalls.title: Assuming a CSV export truncates at 200 rows
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Believing only the first 200 results are included when exporting a large result set.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: For Counted Test Runs, CSV contains matching results beyond the visible 200 default. Distinguish that table from Execution Runs and test metadata, and verify filter scope.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which distinction between CSV export views is correct?

options.text: Execution Runs exports executions, Counted Test Runs exports runs, and Test Library exports test metadata.
Only from the project's Settings page.
Only from a single test's Properties panel.
CSV export is not available in Testim.

practiceQuiz.hint: The views do not all contain the same type of row.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Choose the view for the required data: grouped execution results, individual counted-run results or test metadata. CSV from the Test Library is not automatically the same run-result table.

optionExplanations.A: The export views have different row scopes.
optionExplanations.B: Export is not confined to Settings.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Counted Test Runs has 500 matching available results under the selected filters. What does the documented CSV download include?
practiceQuiz.rationale: The Test Runs guide documents that CSV includes matching results beyond the visible 200 default. This is scoped to available counted-run data and active filters.

optionExplanations.A: The visible default is not the Counted Runs CSV limit.
optionExplanations.B: All 500 matching available results are included by the documented export behavior.
optionExplanations.C: The source does not describe random sampling.
optionExplanations.D: The source supports more than 200 matching results.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What is the PDF export of test results best suited for?

options.text: A raw, machine-parseable data dump for scripting.
Sharing a report of the selected run, without claiming complete project or requirement coverage.
Replacing the CLI for running tests.

practiceQuiz.hint: Think about the audience — stakeholders, not scripts.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Generate PDF run report provides a shareable run artifact. Report generation does not execute tests, edit definitions or establish complete requirements coverage.

optionExplanations.A: This describes raw-data consumption rather than the stated report use.
optionExplanations.B: The run artifact can be shared without certifying complete coverage.
optionExplanations.C: Export does not replace the execution runner.
optionExplanations.D: Reporting does not edit test steps.

quickRecap.value: CSV rows depend on view and filters; Counted Test Runs can export matching results beyond 200.
Generate PDF run report shares the selected run, not a coverage certification.
